question: Which annotation marks a class as a Spring-managed service bean?
discussion: Selected Answer: A @Service is a specialization of @Component for the service layer.
Selected Answer: A @Entity is JPA, @ControllerAdvice handles controller advice, @Mapper is MyBatis.

question: Which annotation lets Spring inject a bean dependency automatically?
discussion: Selected Answer: B @Autowired injects a bean by type (optionally with @Qualifier to disambiguate).
Selected Answer: B @Inject and @Resource also work, but @Autowired is Spring's own annotation.

question: What is the default scope of a Spring bean?
discussion: Selected Answer: A By default, one shared instance of a bean is created per container.
Selected Answer: A @Scope("prototype") creates a new instance each time.

question: Which annotation marks the main class of a Spring Boot application?
discussion: Selected Answer: C @SpringBootApplication combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan.
Selected Answer: C It is placed on the class containing the main method.

question: What is the effect of @RestController?

options.A: It combines @Controller and @ResponseBody so methods return data directly

discussion: Selected Answer: A @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody; return values are serialized (e.g. JSON).
Selected Answer: A It is the standard annotation for REST APIs.

question: Which annotation maps HTTP GET requests to a handler method?
discussion: Selected Answer: B @GetMapping is a shortcut for @RequestMapping(method = GET).
Selected Answer: B Each HTTP verb has a composed annotation.

question: What does @Transactional do on a service method?

options.C: It manages the database transaction around the method

discussion: Selected Answer: C @Transactional begins a transaction and commits/rolls back based on the outcome.
Selected Answer: C By default it rolls back on RuntimeException/Error.

question: Which file is the default source of external configuration in Spring Boot?
discussion: Selected Answer: A application.properties / application.yml are loaded automatically from the classpath.
Selected Answer: A Profile-specific files such as application-dev.properties are also supported.

question: What is a Spring Boot starter?

options.D: A dependency descriptor that aggregates commonly used libraries

discussion: Selected Answer: D Starters (e.g. spring-boot-starter-web) bring in a coherent set of dependencies.
Selected Answer: D They simplify dependency management.

question: Which annotation injects a value from the application configuration?
discussion: Selected Answer: B @Value("${app.name}") injects a property value (with optional defaults).
Selected Answer: B @ConfigurationProperties is a type-safe alternative.

question: Choose two Spring stereotype annotations.
discussion: Selected Answer: AC @Component and @Repository are stereotypes; @Service and @Controller are also stereotypes.
Selected Answer: AC @Bean declares a bean method and @Scope changes scope — neither is a stereotype.

question: What is the purpose of the @Bean annotation?

options.A: It declares a bean inside a @Configuration class
options.B: It marks a class for component scanning

discussion: Selected Answer: A @Bean on a method tells Spring to register the returned object as a bean.
Selected Answer: A It is used for explicit, programmatic bean definitions.

question: Which Spring module simplifies database access with ORM and repositories?
discussion: Selected Answer: B Spring Data JPA provides repository abstractions over JPA/Hibernate.
Selected Answer: B CrudRepository and JpaRepository reduce boilerplate data access code.

question: Which annotation binds a URL path segment to a method parameter?
discussion: Selected Answer: C @PathVariable binds /users/{id} to a parameter.
Selected Answer: C @RequestParam binds query parameters, @RequestBody binds the body.

question: In Spring's Inversion of Control container, who is responsible for creating and wiring beans?

options.A: The developer manually instantiates every object

discussion: Selected Answer: B The ApplicationContext creates beans and injects their dependencies.
Selected Answer: B This is the core idea of IoC/DI in Spring.
